content.title: About
content.content: Toasted bread with potato is a popular snack consisting of a slice of bread topped with a thin layer of boiled potato and toasted until golden. It combines the crisp texture of bread with the soft, slightly sweet flavor of potato.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Toasted bread with potato is often served in cafés and cafeterias as a quick bite.
The tradition of pairing bread and potato dates back to medieval European cuisines where potato was used as a filling for bread.
When properly prepared, the product retains up to 30% of the vitamin C from the potato.
In some regions spices such as rosemary or paprika are added to enhance the taste.
The snack is commonly packaged in single‑serve portions, making it popular in the food‑service industry.

items.title: Source of complex carbohydrates
items.content: Both bread and potato provide slowly digestible carbs that supply steady energy and help maintain blood‑sugar levels.

items.title: Rich in dietary fiber
items.content: Potato, especially when the skin is retained, contributes fiber that supports digestive health.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Bread supplies B1, B3 and folate, which are essential for metabolic processes.

items.title: Minerals
items.content: The snack provides potassium, magnesium and iron, supporting muscle and nerve function.

items.title: Low in fat
items.content: When prepared without added oil, toasted bread with potato remains a low‑fat option.

items.title: Gluten allergy
items.content: Bread contains gluten, which can trigger reactions in people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Sodium content
items.content: If salt is added to the potato topping, monitor the amount to avoid excessive sodium intake.

items.title: Bacterial growth risk
items.content: When kept at room temperature for more than 2 hours, moisture from the potato can promote bacterial growth.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: Although not fatty, the carbohydrate load can be high; portion control is advisable for weight‑management diets.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Toasted bread with potato can be enjoyed as a standalone snack, served with sauces such as sour cream or mustard, or used as a base for open‑face sandwiches. Reheat in a toaster or oven to achieve a crisp crust.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the product in an airtight container in the refrigerator at 0 °C – +4 °C. For longer storage (more than 5 days) reheat before consumption. Discard if it develops an off‑odor, discoloration, or visible mold.
